evidence: The round-0 hunk strips the prefix with strings.TrimPrefix(..., 'all:') before addEmbedded walks a directory unfiltered, so a bare-directory embed would admit _/. files the compiler omits; by 3753bdc addEmbedded takes an 'all bool' and the reply shows the SkipDir filter, and the agent's compiler check (dir embed omits sub/_x.txt, glob d/* embeds it) matches go:embed semantics.
guidance_note: When a parser strips a prefix that changes semantics (all:), carry it as a field on the parsed value rather than discarding it at the first read.

evidence: ShippedText parsed every .go file with no //go:build evaluation; the reply concedes clone_other.go and detach_posix.go were mishandled and that the first fix (evaluating once with every tag but ignore true) inverted negation, replaced by satisfiability enumeration in neverBuilt.
guidance_note: When mirroring a toolchain rule such as build-constraint selection, enumerate the accept/reject table (negation, legacy +build, blank-line placement, contradictory lines) and test each against `go list` before writing the predicate, instead of fixing one spelling per round.

evidence: The CHANGELOG said 'every message this protects is an error-path string' while ShippedText's comment says 'most' and the manifest carries 'Initialized lit workspace'; e106b35 changes it to 'most'. Flag is a false positive: the 3753bdc diff shows 'every message' on both the removed and added line, so the sentence predates the review and 3753bdc only edited other clauses.
guidance_note: Before shipping a changelog entry that restates code comments, diff each quantified claim (every, cannot, all) against the comment it paraphrases.

evidence: Literal text and asset paths share one map with plain assignment, and disjointness rested only on literals needing a space; the agent kept one key space (a claim carries no kind) and routed both writers through Corpus.add, which errors when a handle maps to two bodies, which removes the silent clobber the reviewer described. Flag is a false positive: the shared map and plain writes are original design, not introduced by 3753bdc.
guidance_note: When two producers write one keyed map, route both through a constructor that refuses a conflicting key, rather than relying on an incidental property of the keys.

evidence: 3753bdc introduced excludedFromEveryBuild, with a doc comment answering F2's platform-variant caveat, and applied it in importsOf and collectFile but not entryPackages, which still parsed PackageClauseOnly; the agent's fix adds ParseComments and the same check. Linking 3753bdc to F2 is inferred from that doc comment, since no reply names it as F2's fix.
guidance_note: When adding a new file-selection predicate, grep every reader that parses the same files (entryPackages, importsOf, collectFile) and apply it at all of them in the same commit.

evidence: The hunk shows the Reanchored report printed before os.WriteFile under a comment saying it 'reports an action already taken'; the fix moves the report after the write and TestWriteReportsAReanchorAndStillWrites pins the order. Flag false positive: e106b35 only edited the CHANGELOG 'every'->'most', and write()'s re-anchor report came from the agent's own internal-review commit, not a packet finding's fix.
guidance_note: When a comment asserts a past-tense action, place the print after the call that performs it and test the ordering in the same commit.

evidence: The CHANGELOG said 1,102 while the merged manifest had 1,104 (the master merge moved 1,102->1,104), and the agent found 269 was really 272; it dropped the volatile figures, which is one of the two remedies the reviewer offered. Flag false positive: e106b35 changed only 'every'->'most' in that sentence, and the stale count came from the manifest regeneration at the master merge, not from F3's fix. The removal missed copies, though; see F16 and F17.
guidance_note: Do not write a count of generated output into hand-written prose; if a figure is needed, state it once at the measurement site and grep the repo for every copy when removing it.

evidence: docclaims-sync imports internal/docclaims, which contains manifest_gen.go, so a corrupted manifest blocks its own repair; the agent confirmed this and noted deleting the file also fails, then deferred to ticket links-doc-v1-49pz because it is tool robustness needing new go/parser code. Deferring with a filed ticket that has a concrete shape is defensible scope control. Flag false positive: the import existed since the tool was written, and e106b35 only touched CHANGELOG.
guidance_note: When adding a generator, copy the sibling generator's structural guarantees (tools/lawtokens-sync's TestToolDoesNotCompileTheFileItWrites) at creation rather than learning them from review.

evidence: The reviewer's blank-line rule is false for //go:build but true for // +build, which it also named. The agent tested only //go:build ('go build ./... succeeds') and declined, then in F15 admitted via `go list` that '// +build ignore' with no blank line is INCLUDED, so the decline left a real bug for another round. Flag false positive: excludedFromEveryBuild's comment scan predates e106b35, a CHANGELOG-only commit.
guidance_note: When disproving a finding by experiment, vary every input the finding names (here both //go:build and // +build spellings) before declining; a one-point measurement cannot refute a two-spelling claim.

evidence: Matched called tightest once per undeduplicated span; the agent measured 1,197 of 7,073 repeated texts and 506ms->417ms after a per-call memo, and the 0a10c14 diff shows the answered map scoped inside Matched with a byte-identical manifest. Flag false positive: Matched's loop predates e106b35.

Only the clean and Stopped paths of write() were tested; 0a10c14 adds TestWriteReportsAReanchorAndStillWrites, which constructs an AnchorMoved-only Comparison and asserts the write happened with the new Src, and mutation runs show it kills a widened refusal. Flag false positive: the untested branch came from an internal-review commit, not from e106b35.
guidance_note: When a function gains a branch whose whole point is to differ from its neighbour, add a test per branch in that commit, and do the same for every other function that switches on the same classification (verify as well as write).

evidence: The e106b35 hunk shows verify counting `d.Kind == docclaims.AnchorMoved` inline while Reanchored() exists for that purpose; the fix replaces it with len(cmp.Reanchored()). The reply-hint says pushback but the reply concedes and fixes. Flag false positive: the inline count predates e106b35.
guidance_note: After introducing a classification accessor, grep for the raw Kind comparison it replaces and convert every call site in the same commit.

evidence: The writer printed d.Now with %q while Explain truncated via ellipsis(d.Now,120); ellipsis is unexported, so the agent added Drift.NowBrief() used by both Explain and the writer instead of duplicating the rule, and pinned it with a 4KB handle test. Flag false positive: the print came from the internal-review re-anchor report commit, not e106b35.
guidance_note: When a new report renders a value an existing formatter already shapes, put the shaping on the value's type and call it from both, rather than formatting inline.

evidence: F11's fix in 0a10c14 tested write()'s re-anchor branch only, while verify() switches on the same Stopped/Reanchored classification and had only its fallback tested; 6bcf029 adds TestVerifyGivesEachCaseItsOwnRemedy and a precedence test. The agent also pinned stopped-beats-moved precedence, which the reviewer had not asked for.
guidance_note: When a finding says one consumer of a classification lacks branch tests, sweep every consumer of that classification (write and verify) in the same fix.

evidence: The reviewer's concrete example ('//go:build ignore' with no blank line is not a constraint) is wrong per the agent's `go list` table, but the rule holds for '// +build'; 6bcf029 applies blank(c.End()) only in the IsPlusBuild case, with seven go-list-derived test placements. Not fix-caused: this re-raises F9, which the agent wrongly declined, and 0a10c14 (the memo and write tests) did not touch excludedFromEveryBuild. The round was spent because of a bad pushback, not a bad fix.
guidance_note: Settle toolchain-behaviour questions with the tool's own inclusion report (`go list -f '{{.GoFiles}}'`) across every spelling the first time a finding raises them, so a declined finding cannot come back as a confirmed one.

evidence: F7's fix removed the volatile manifest counts but left 'eighteen documented error messages' hand-copied in CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG and docclaims.go; the 6bcf029 diff shows CONTRIBUTING's 'eighteen' removed, and the agent says 'I fixed that one and walked straight past this one'.
guidance_note: When a finding says one measured number is duplicated across prose, grep the PR's prose for every digit or spelled-out count and give each one a single home in the same commit.

evidence: F7's fix turned '269 of the 1,102 entries' into 'hundreds of entries' but left 'and one sits in 29 of them' in the CHANGELOG and Claim.Src, and the 6bcf029 diff shows the CHANGELOG tail dropped and the AnchorMoved comment pointing to Claim.Src; the agent says 'you caught me doing the job by halves'.
guidance_note: When removing a duplicated measurement, remove the whole clause it lives in from every non-owning copy, not only the part the finding quoted.

evidence: The reviewer re-raises F8 and explicitly asks whether the deferral stands; the agent confirms the ticket links-doc-v1-49pz and gives the same reasoning. Flag false positive: 6bcf029 did not touch main.go's imports, and the coupling dates from the tool's creation.

CONTRIBUTING and CHANGELOG claim deletion 'cannot be masked by an unrelated string', but Claim.Src's own comment says an asset anchor lets a stray recurrence keep a deleted sentence green. F3's fix corrected one prose overclaim against a code comment in this same CHANGELOG entry without sweeping the entry's other absolute claims; the text predates 6bcf029, which touched only adjacent lines.
guidance_note: When a finding shows one sentence of a doc entry overclaiming against the code's own comments, audit every absolute claim in that entry and its CONTRIBUTING twin against those comments before replying.

evidence: The comment 'The exit line counts what actually differs' governed a switch whose moved>0 line counted only re-anchors in a mixed comparison. The agent rejected folding in the QuoteDropped count (a total under a re-anchor sentence) and made each line state its scope as '%d of %d', moving the comment onto the fallback. Flag false positive: the F14 hunk at 0a10c14 already shows the switch and comment, so 6bcf029 did not create the drift; the branches came from an internal-review commit.
guidance_note: When adding branches beside a commented line, re-read the comment above them and narrow it to the line it describes in the same commit.

evidence: The agent confirmed with go/ast that the TestUnclosedFenceIsAnError rationale merged into TestACollidingHandleIsRefusedRatherThanOverwritten's doc comment, and moved it in 9e97997. The packet does not show which commit inserted the collision test; its name matches F4's fix (9942a88), but that diff is absent, so causation is unverified. The 6bcf029 test diff edits lines 302+, not this block.
guidance_note: When inserting a new test between existing ones, check that the comment block directly above the insertion point still attaches to the function it describes.

narrative: A 3,900-line gate PR reviewed by CoPirate across five rounds until it hit the round cap, with the agent also running about ten internal review rounds in parallel. Most bot findings were real and well handled, often with measured evidence and mutation tests. Round 3 was entirely avoidable: F16 and F17 are the unswept remainder of F7's count removal, F14 is F11's missing-branch-test gap in verify(), and F15 re-raises F9, which the agent declined on a one-spelling experiment. The PR shipped repeated prose overclaims about itself (F3, F7, F16, F17, F19), the same drift class the gate exists to catch.
guidance_observations: Each fix for a duplicated-number or overclaiming-prose finding addressed only the quoted instance; a grep of the PR's prose for counts and absolute words after the first such finding would have closed F16, F17 and F19 in one round.
The agent's own pushback on F9 was disproved by its own later measurement; a decline based on an experiment should vary every input the finding names, because a wrong decline costs a full round.

Many ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flags here are false positives because the named commits (e106b35 CHANGELOG-only, 0a10c14 memo and tests) did not touch the flagged code; the real churn came from internal-review commits that the GitHub threads never named.
The CHANGELOG entry grew into a multi-thousand-word narrative restating code comments, which multiplied the copies of each fact and so the drift findings against it.
